title: Maximum Capacity Within Budget
summary: Given arrays costs and capacity of length n, and an integer budget, select at most two distinct machines with a total cost less than budget to maximize the total capacity.
statement: Given arrays costs and capacity of length n, and an integer budget, select at most two distinct machines with a total cost less than budget to maximize the total capacity.
constraints: costs and capacity have equal length up to 100,000.
Choose zero, one, or two distinct machines whose total cost is strictly less than budget.
reference_solution:
def maximum_machine_capacity(costs,capacity,budget):
    from bisect import bisect_left
    items=sorted((costs[i],capacity[i],i) for i in range(len(costs)));ordered_cost=[item[0] for item in items]
    top=[];prefix=[]
    for cost,value,index in items:
        top=sorted(top+[(value,index)],reverse=True)[:2];prefix.append(top[:])
    answer=max((value for cost,value,_ in items if cost<budget),default=0)
    for cost,value,index in items:
        limit=bisect_left(ordered_cost,budget-cost)
        if not limit:continue
        candidates=prefix[limit-1]
        partner=next((other for other,other_index in candidates if other_index!=index),None)
        if partner is not None:answer=max(answer,value+partner)
    return answer

For each machine, binary-search the prefix with partner cost strictly below budget-current cost.
Choose the best prefix capacity whose original index differs, and also consider every affordable singleton.
Every legal pair is considered when either member is the current machine, while the two prefix leaders suffice after excluding at most one index.
